title: Grove's swap burst caps are tuned per pool while the daily throughput slope is held constant across pools
content:
Three Curve swap instances share two of their three parameters and differ in the third. AUSD/USDC (A...6.4.2.4.3) and PYUSD/USDS (A...6.6.2.4.3) both set `maxAmount` 5,000,000 with a 100,000,000-per-day slope and 0.1% `maxSlippage`. RLUSD/USDC (A...6.1.2.4.3) sets `maxAmount` 20,000,000 with the same slope and the same slippage.

The division of labour between the two limit parameters becomes clear when read across pools. `slope` is a throughput budget — how much converting Grove may do in a day — and that is a statement about Grove, so it is the same everywhere. `maxAmount` is a per-execution size cap, and price impact for a given trade size depends entirely on the depth of the specific pool, so it is the parameter that must be calibrated per venue. A 0.1% slippage tolerance is only achievable in a thin pool at a smaller size, which is why the two newer pairs get a quarter of RLUSD/USDC's cap.

The same pool can also carry both limit shapes for different activities. The Curve RLUSD/USDC pool has a swap instance with the burst shape and a separate "LP Deposits" instance (A...6.3) with `maxAmount` 25,000,000 and a 25,000,000-per-day slope — a one-day refill, the accumulation shape — plus its own distinct inflow and outflow RateLimitIDs (A...6.3.2.3.1, A...6.3.2.3.2). Holding liquidity in a pool and trading through it are budgeted independently because they are different exposures.

One reconciliation hazard: the swap budget is filed under a dedicated "Swap RateLimitID" for RLUSD/USDC but under "Inflow RateLimitID" for AUSD/USDC and PYUSD/USDS, whose outflow IDs read `N/A` while their deposit and withdrawal limits read `N/A - swaps only` (A...6.4.2.3, A...6.6.2.3). The same role is recorded under two different field names, so the register cannot be reconciled to on-chain keys by field name alone.
description: AUSD/USDC and PYUSD/USDS allow 5 million per burst against RLUSD/USDC's 20 million, all three with a 100 million per day slope and 0.1% max slippage.
